messages.subject: telling stan to save things
parts:
I have a stan model with parameters real mu and real theta3[J3]. I want to create the foliowing:

for (j in 1:J3)
theta3_adj[j] <- theta3[j] - mu;

This seems to work fine, as long as I define theta3_adj within the "model" statement (not the "parameters"). That's fine. But then when stan is done, it does not seem to have saved theta3_adj. That's a bummer cos the only reason I created theta3_adj was to save it!

Also, I tried the following:

for (j in 1:J3)
theta3_dif[j] <- theta3[j] - mean(theta3);

But it didn't work.

A

> Given that we have the Bugs models conveniently on the website, I retract my request to have them all in a pdf file. I

>
> The current Stan homepage is just full of stuff but not particualrly user-oriented.
> The googlecode page is fine but I think it would help to have a super-clean homepage.

I agree that we need to make this easier for users
who aren't used to open-source code projects.

Maybe you want a separate Stan and RStan page. Otherwise,
things are going to get complicated if we have all of our
interfaces (we have R for some statisticians, but have toyed
with doing stata, too; we need Python for the hackers and MATLAB
for the engineers/coputer scientists).

So the Stan home page could just point to a separate
"using Stan from R" sub page.

The things I thought were critical are in the right column
under "Stan". Do you think we can remove any of that
to make it cleaner?

I'd be happy getting rid of "how to cite Stan", which is up
there because Andrew wanted it in the first place! I also
don't think we need the blog links.

We could move everything one level down and just have
links. So "Get Involved" could point to a "Get Involved"
page, etc. That makes it cleaner at the expense of requiring
more nav clicks by the user. Ditto for "Contact", but that
may not be enough of a name to indicate its contents for those
not used to open-source projects.

If you want clean, you also need to REMOVE things.

Here's where these things are now and what I think
we could add:
> - Instructions for setting up Stan
In the Stan User's Guide. Need to be pulled up.
> - Instructions for setting up Stan from R

In the "RStan Getting Started Guide". Maybe we should
change the name to "RStan Installation and Getting Started Guide"?
Or should we have two links? A whole sub-heading about
installation?

> - Stan manual

There's a clear link under Documentation. At least it seems
clear to me.

> - Bugs examples

That's not on the home page.

> - Stan mailing lists

These are listed under "Groups" on the links page, where they
always are for Google Code projects (not that R/BUGS users
would realize that), but they're also under the "Contact" heading
on the right.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Stan Home Page contents
parts:
I'm happy to create a Stan home page.

URL:

I like "mc-stan.org". Is everyone else OK with that?

We'll want mc-stan.com, too, so it can forward.

How do I create this and bill it to the project? Who
should the registrar be?


MAIL:

Then we can set up mail for various features at mc-stan.org
and make sure they get routed to the right person. As of
now, we're using mc-sta...@gmail.com as the single e-mail
contact that forwards to me and Daniel. (We can set it up
to forward to a wider audience if anyone else wants in.)


HOME PAGE:

I can layout the HTML, but the issue is what should be
on the page. Andrew suggests 5 or so lines that are
really important. That means we're going to have to
do some re-org and re-thinking.

With a separate home page, the "Google Code" home page
function changes. Let's think top-down from the Stan
home page. I find the best way to do this is to consider
who might be visiting it and what they might want.

At the very least, I see users coming in for the
latest C++/command-line or R code, wanting to know
where to report bugs or contact us via e-mail.

Here's what's there now:

* Description of what Stan is (must be suitable for all users,
or allow quick triage of users to their appropriate 2nd
tier page)

* Status indication of latest version
(perhaps implicit in a link to code, etc.?)

* Link to getting started docs
a. C++
b. command-line
c. RStan

* Links to manuals
a. C++ API
b. Modeling Language + Command Line
c. RStan

* Links to code downloads
a. latest RStan
b. latest C++/command-line Stan

* Links to mailing lists
a. Stan Users' Group
b. Stan Developers' Group
c. Stan Announce
d. Stan BuildBot Status

* License Info
a. Stan (BSD)
b. RStan (GPL)
c. Eigen (LGPL), Boost (Boost License)

* Contact e-mail

* About
a. who wrote it
b. who funded it

* Links for Issue Tracking
a. reporting BUGS
b. suggesting features

* Get Involved
a. contribute patches or more code
b. contribute a model

* How to Cite Stan

Things Andrew suggested adding:

* Link to BUGS models

Things people have suggested removing:

:-)

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Stan Eigen vs. RcppEigen, versions and licenses
parts:
RStan is using RcppEigen. The RcppEigen CRAN page's
NEWS as of 2012-06-26 indicates Eigen 3.1.0.

If we upgrade Stan's version of Eigen to 3.1.1, we
have to support multiple versions of Eigen.

As I've said before, I would very strongly prefer it if
we could distribute our own version of Eigen with RStan.
I believe the main issue before was size for CRAN, but
if we're skipping CRAN. So does anyone object to including
the same Eigen in RStan as we use in C++ Stan?

At least this compatibility issue is backward. In
RcppEigen version 0.2.0 they were using Eigen version
3.1.0-alpha2. I'd rather not have to support prototypes.
Maybe things will settle down RcppEigen ever gets to
version 1? Or is this just another CS/stats difference
(numbering versions from 1/0 and arrays from 0/1)?

- Bob

CRAN.  CRAN says the boost package is 404 since boost-1.0.0
in 2004:

Mav and I had discussed this on the list. The boost R package is abandoned, but the CRAN servers have some version of Boost on them. Presumably, this is the version of Boost in the Debian testing repository, which is 1.49. Thus, if the version of Boost that CRAN has is sufficient to build stanc (and thus RStan), it is possible to require that a particular version of Boost be available on the system to compile the models.

Conceivably, we could do the same thing with Eigen. Depend on RcppEigen so that the CRAN servers can build RStan but require a particular version of the Eigen headers be available on the system to compile the models.

That is always available as a fallback plan, although it seems confusing to users. There is no law that says we can't also host a giant version of RStan on GoogleCode that has all of Boost and Eigen in rstan/inst/include for people who are unable to follow instructions for how to install Boost and / or Eigen themselves.

I don't know that much about Boost, but I still think it is feasible for (R)Stan to support whatever version of Eigen RcppEigen has at the moment and whatever is the latest stable Eigen on the Eigen website. Most of the time, they won't diverge that much, and if there is something in (R)Stan that works with one but not the other, then we would want to know about it because it is probably a regression.

Ben

parts:
Hi, Bob.

1. mc-stan.org is good for me.

2. Here's what I would put on the home page:
a. One or two-sentence description of Stan along with the logo
b. Status indication of latest version (e.g., "Latest versions: Stan1.03 released 9 Aug 2012, Rstan 1.1 released 10 Aug 2012")
c. Link to instructions: How to install Stan through R
d. Link to instructions: How to install Stan to run directly
e. Link to Stan manual
f. Link to page with Stan examples
g. For more: link to googlecode page
h. How to join the user group [with a note that info on the developer group is on the googlecode page]

3. I don't think we need most of the other things in your list below. We don't need to link to the Rstan manual, that link can be on the "How to install Stan through R directly" page. We don't need to link to C++ API, that can be on the googlecode page. We don't need to link to the licence info, that can be on the googlecode page. Etc.

I am happy to have the google code page be as crowded as you'd like. But I'd like the homepage to be clean. Users like me would liek the manual, the installation instructions, the examples, and to see whether anything is new. More sophisticated people can go to the googlecode page. Thus, I'm not suggesting to remove any info, I just want to create a clean friendly portal. Right now, I'm in the stan project but I had difficulty finding what I need.

Does that make sense?
A
